definitions.explanation: An intense, persistent fear of a specific object or situation, strong enough to interfere with daily life. Used as a standalone noun and as a suffix on the feared thing.

examples.japanese: かれは{高所|こうしょ}{恐怖症|きょうふしょう}だ。
examples.english: He has a fear of heights.

examples.japanese: {閉所|へいしょ}{恐怖症|きょうふしょう}でエレベーターが{苦手|にがて}だ。
examples.english: I have claustrophobia, so I'm not good with elevators.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どものころの{経験|けいけん}が{原因|げんいん}で、{犬|いぬ}に{対|たい}する{恐怖症|きょうふしょう}になった。
examples.english: Because of a childhood experience, I developed a phobia of dogs.

notes:
Most commonly used as a suffix on the feared object or situation (X{恐怖症|きょうふしょう}). A medical term that is also used loosely in everyday speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高所|こうしょ}{恐怖症|きょうふしょう}: fear of heights (acrophobia)
- {閉所|へいしょ}{恐怖症|きょうふしょう}: claustrophobia
- {対人|たいじん}{恐怖症|きょうふしょう}: social phobia
- {先端|せんたん}{恐怖症|きょうふしょう}: fear of pointed objects

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {恐怖|きょうふ}: fear; terror — the emotion itself, without the sense of a disorder
- トラウマ: trauma — a damaging past experience, which can be a cause of a {恐怖症|きょうふしょう}
